children: Britain's main stock indexes were heading for weekly gains on Friday, as investors sought refuge in defensive sectors from a rout in AI-linked equities globally, while a dip in bond yields boosted risk sentiment ahead of next week's inflation figures.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
edged 0.08% lower to 10,831.70 points by 10:12 GMT, but was on track for its best week since early April, while the midcap FTSE 250
rose 0.55%.
The defensive healthcare sector was set for a nearly 5% gain for the week, despite falling over 1% on Friday
Drugmakers AstraZeneca
and GSK
fell 1.8% and 1%, respectively, on the day
The personal goods sector (.FTNMX402040) was up 7.2% for the week
Heavily weighted banks slipped on Friday after the Guardian reported British finance minister John Healey was set to tax the lenders in the budget later this month
"While big international banks in the UK are likely to be less affected, domestic names are in the firing line," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, in a note
NatWest Group
and Lloyds Banking
were down 2.2% each
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said signs of second-round inflation were limited ahead of next week's data release for September
Traders are pricing in four BoE rate hikes over the next 12 months, according to LSEG data
The UK's 10-year benchmark yields were heading for weekly declines after three straight weeks of gains
Defence stocks (.FTNMX502010) helped limit the losses on Friday: BAE Systems
, Melrose Industries
and Babcock International
rose between 1.5% and 3.7%
E-commerce group THG
rose 6.7%, extending a surge of 16% on Thursday after it raised its annual adjusted core profit forecast
